title: Onimusha: Way of the Sword Demo
provenance: Reported by flacknabe-cpu (highball-db#450, 2026-10-11), Apple M1 Pro, macOS 26.7, Highball 0.10.14, engine x64-sikarugir10.0_6-r24, the game on D3DMetal in a DXMT environment, 60 fps cap, rated 3 of 5 after 19 minutes, the game's benchmark at 11341 points and 32 fps on average with a modified D3DMetal. flacknabe-cpu again (highball-db#450, 2026-10-16): Highball 0.10.16, engine x64-crossover26.3-r25, the original D3DMetal 3, HB_TSSHIM_ATOMIC64=1, the demo launches and reaches gameplay on the M1 Pro. Not verified by the maintainer. udance4ever (highball-db#450, 2026-11-15): Play applied the recipe (the Wine 11 engine and HB_TSSHIM_ATOMIC64=1), 58 minutes of play, up to the fight with Ganryu. At the first launch Steam's licence agreement for the demo didn't show, Steam's window staying black under D3DMetal. The player set the game's graphics mode to DXMT, which let Steam draw the agreement, accepted it, ended the wait with Stop (Stop all Windows processes didn't end Highball's wait for the game), set the mode back to the environment's and pressed Play again. Not verified by the maintainer.
notes: Capcom's RE Engine, DirectX 12. On an M1 Pro it stops with an unsupported graphics card error, because D3DMetal answers no to the game's check for 64-bit atomics on descriptor heap resources (D3D12 OPTIONS11), the same check that blocks Kunitsu-Gami. A player got it running, through its benchmark at 32 fps, by patching D3DMetal itself so the check says yes. Highball cannot ship a modified D3DMetal, so out of the box it does not start on an M1. On an M4 D3DMetal 3 already answers yes (measured here 2026-10-14 with a probe). On Highball's Wine 11 engine r25 (0.10.16) the variable HB_TSSHIM_ATOMIC64=1 makes Highball's DirectX 12 layer answer yes, and the demo reaches gameplay on the M1 Pro with the original D3DMetal (confirmed by the reporter, highball-db#450). The recipe sets both; the game's benchmark has its own page. PRAGMATA SKETCHBOOK's demo stops at the same check and ran with the same D3DMetal patch (highball-db#485). A second player played 58 minutes with the recipe. On Wine 11 Steam's licence agreement for the demo stayed invisible at the first launch, because Steam's window can't draw under D3DMetal there, and the game's graphics mode on DXMT for that one launch got past it (highball-db#450, see the known issues).

knownIssues.symptom: Unsupported graphics card error at start, then the game quits (M1 Pro)
knownIssues.cause: D3DMetal reports AtomicInt64OnDescriptorHeapResourceSupported as false, and the game requires it
knownIssues.fix: the recipe: Wine 11 engine r25 or later with HB_TSSHIM_ATOMIC64=1, which has Highball's layer in front of D3DMetal answer yes (confirmed on an M1 Pro, highball-db#450)

knownIssues.symptom: At the first launch nothing happens: Steam's window is black and the demo never starts (Wine 11 engine, D3DMetal)
knownIssues.cause: Steam waits for its licence agreement for the demo, and on the Wine 11 engines Steam's window can't draw under D3DMetal, so the agreement stays invisible
knownIssues.fix: the player's way (highball-db#450): set the game's graphics mode to DXMT on its page, press Play and accept the agreement in Steam's window, press Stop, set the mode back to the environment's and press Play again
